**Exit gate:** B33 conserva grafo/filtragem com isolamento profundo, mutation/race
e redução medida de alocações/RAM; bytes/pins/waiters têm orçamento por worktree

expansão total desnecessária ou cache de autorização stale. Git reader fica scoped.

**Exit gate:** B35 qualifica handshake user/worktree/Git/engine/schema, endpoint
protegido, lifecycle/restart/update e fallback CI/standalone. Stdio não é IPC
compartilhável; watcher é hint, writers publicam geração e efeitos ambíguos exigem
receipt antes de retry. CPU/jobs simultâneos preservam query/QoS/output determinístico
com RAM/CPU/latência por cenário, sem scheduler/agents/workflows automáticos no core.

- Manter draft durante a escrita; executar somente com escopo autorizado.
- Qualificar todos os deltas obrigatórios antes de encerrar o programa.
- Preservar verdict, coverage, bindings e limites de cada operação; latência menor não comprova eficácia universal.
- Conservar benchmarks isolados, resultados e erros; não restaurar trabalho do operador para medir.
- Adotar residência somente pelo contrato/qualificação correspondente, sem inferir que MCP stdio é IPC compartilhável.

115	## 7. Final Report
116	
117	### Delivered scope
118	Runtime opcional por worktree: identidade (usuário, worktree canônico, diretório comum do Git), endpoint em socket Unix 0600 num diretório 0700 do usuário com verificação de credencial do par, handshake que recusa outro engine/build/protocolo/schema por campo, ciclo de vida `serve|start|attach|status|stop|restart` com drenagem, timeout de ociosidade e época nova a cada início, e o comportamento standalone sem autostart (R1-R4, R9). Fora: operações do domínio e cache (próxima spec), QoS e medição (a seguinte), named pipe do Windows.

13	// ResidentGitMemo keeps, in a process that outlives one operation, the output of the Git reads
14	// that are pure functions of object ids or of the commit HEAD named when they ran (see
15	// governancePureGitRead). It is off unless a process turns it on, so nothing changes for a
16	// command that runs once; the optional worktree runtime turns it on (spec
17	// pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache). A hit is the answer Git would give: the key
18	// holds the commit and the shallow state, and the output of such a read cannot differ for them.
19	type ResidentGitMemo struct {
20		mu      sync.Mutex
21		max     int64
22		bytes   int64
23		entries map[string]*list.Element
24		order   *list.List // front is the most recently used
25		hits    atomic.Int64
26		misses  atomic.Int64
27	}
28	
29	type residentGitEntry struct {
30		key    string
31		stdout []byte
32	}
33	
34	var residentGit atomic.Pointer[ResidentGitMemo]
35	
36	// EnableResidentGitMemo turns the memo on with a byte budget for what it retains.
37	func EnableResidentGitMemo(maxBytes int64) *ResidentGitMemo {
38		m := &ResidentGitMemo{max: maxBytes, entries: map[string]*list.Element{}, order: list.New()}
39		residentGit.Store(m)
40		return m
41	}
42	
43	// DisableResidentGitMemo turns the memo off and drops what it held.
44	func DisableResidentGitMemo() { residentGit.Store(nil) }
45	
46	// ResidentGitMemoStats are the hits, misses, entries and retained bytes since it was enabled.
47	func ResidentGitMemoStats() (hits, misses int64, entries int, bytes int64) {
48		m := residentGit.Load()
49		if m == nil {
50			return 0, 0, 0, 0
51		}
52		m.mu.Lock()
53		defer m.mu.Unlock()
54		return m.hits.Load(), m.misses.Load(), len(m.entries), m.bytes
55	}
56	
57	// residentGitKey names a read: the root, the commit it was made at (empty for a read by object
58	// id), the shallow state of the repository and the exact command. A root whose Git directory
59	// is not a plain .git directory is not memoized: its shallow state is not read here.
60	func residentGitKey(root, head string, args []string) (string, bool) {
61		gitDir := filepath.Join(root, ".git")
62		info, err := os.Lstat(gitDir)
63		if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
64			return "", false
65		}
66		shallow := "-"
67		if s, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "shallow")); err == nil {
68			shallow = fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", s.Size(), s.ModTime().UnixNano())
69		}
70		// The repository's own config can change what a read answers (log.follow, for one).
71		config := "-"
72		if c, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(gitDir, "config")); err == nil {
73			config = fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d", c.Size(), c.ModTime().UnixNano())
74		}
75		return strings.Join([]string{filepath.Clean(root), head, shallow, config, strings.Join(args, "\x00")}, "\x01"), true
76	}
77	
78	func (m *ResidentGitMemo) get(key string) ([]byte, bool) {
79		m.mu.Lock()
80		defer m.mu.Unlock()
81		el, ok := m.entries[key]
82		if !ok {
83			m.misses.Add(1)
84			return nil, false
85		}
86		m.order.MoveToFront(el)
87		m.hits.Add(1)
88		return append([]byte(nil), el.Value.(*residentGitEntry).stdout...), true
89	}
90

239	## Amendment: transport, identity and slicing of the worktree runtime (B35)
240	
241	Decided 2026-11-09 with the maintainer, before the functional start of B35:
242	
243	- **Transport.** A stream socket in the user's own directory: a Unix domain socket
244	  (Linux, macOS), mode 0600 in a 0700 directory owned by the user, whose peer is
245	  checked by the operating system's credentials (`SO_PEERCRED`, `LOCAL_PEERCRED`)
246	  before any byte is read. No TCP, no token, no network surface. Windows has no
247	  named-pipe implementation in this repository (the standard library has none and
248	  the repository takes no dependency for it): the runtime reports itself
249	  unsupported there and every command runs standalone. That is a declared
250	  limitation, not a silent one, and a named pipe with the owner's ACL is the
251	  follow-up that lifts it.
252	- **Identity.** user (uid) + canonical worktree (symlinks resolved) + Git common
253	  directory + engine version/build + wire protocol + schema. The endpoint name is
254	  a digest of the location part only (user, worktree, Git common directory), so two
255	  worktrees or two users never share an endpoint; the engine part is compared at the
256	  handshake, field by field, and a difference is refused naming it, so that a new CLI
257	  that finds an old process after an update is refused by name instead of being
258	  given a different endpoint and never learning the old one is there.
259	- **Authority.** The runtime of slice 1 hosts no domain operation: it answers
260	  handshake, status and stop. It confers no authority, signature or presence, and a
261	  client that attaches gains nothing it did not have standalone.
262	- **Slicing.** B35 is delivered in three specs, each reviewed on its own:
263	  `pose-optional-worktree-runtime` (identity, endpoint, handshake, lifecycle,
264	  standalone fallback: R1-R4), `pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache` (R5, R7: the
265	  resident reuse of the B33 views, reconciliation, typed results) and
266	  `pose-worktree-runtime-qos-and-measurement` (R6, R8: budgets, short queries
267	  protected from heavy checks, measured thresholds). Budgets and thresholds are
268	  fixed from a measured synthetic corpus with a declared environment, never from a
269	  historical sample.

I can't approve this milestone. The three member specs are closed and the sealed build and test evidence passes. But I found three medium-severity defects. One is a gap in the exit-gate evidence, one is a decision record (the ADR) that contradicts what was delivered, and one is a race in identity checking that the first spec's D1 test was written to catch.

The shell was denied for every `pose` command, including the required `pose validate --strict --module pose-mcp`. I did not run it myself. Its result below comes from the sealed evidence. Everything else comes from reading the code, the specs, the ADR and the measurement report.

## Criteria

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| exit-gate | **failed (F1)** | The gate asks for "RAM/CPU/latência por cenário" under simultaneous jobs. The measurement records latency per scenario, a single peak RAM figure for the whole run, and no CPU at all. The harness only reads `VmHWM`/`VmRSS` (`pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_measure_test.go:225`). No two heavy jobs run at the same time: the report says the short queries were sequential (`.pose/reports/2026-11-09-pose-worktree-runtime-measurements.md:53,57`). The implementer's notes disclose that CPU *limits* are missing, but not that CPU *measurement* is. The other gate clauses hold: handshake by field (`runtime.go:88-104,426-429`), a 0600 socket in a 0700 directory with the peer's credentials checked (`runtime.go:153-199,404-408`), a new epoch on every start, standalone fallback, stdio not used as IPC, and nothing retried after an unknown outcome (`runtime_host.go:203-216`). |
| integration | **failed (F2, F3)** | The ADR amendment still says the runtime "hosts no domain operation" and that the second slice reuses the B33 graph views. Its decision text also still asks for CPU quotas and a global bound (ADR `:64-65,259-269`). The delivered slices host five checks, memoize Git reads instead, and declare CPU and global limits as non-goals. The ADR is still `Proposed` (`:5`). |
| membership | passed | All three specs have `status: done` and a `completed_at` date. The head commits close the last spec and refresh the indexes. Each spec's integration check is sealed as passing. |
| regression | passed | `unit:pose-mcp/go/test` and `build:pose-mcp/go/build` pass, as do the matrix entries the three slices added. |
| residual-risk | **failed (F6)** | The resident-cache spec keeps an open follow-up of medium severity (`.pose/specs/2026-11-09-pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache.md:137`). The third spec delivered that work, but the follow-up was never disposed, and the review policy only accepts low-severity risks. |
